headline: Long-form fell to 3,567 views on 2026-11-13, its lowest day in two weeks, and the Ravana long-form due 19 November has no draft on disk. The owner's note changes the Tipu Short: the fall of Srirangapatna and who took the treasure, not the birthday. All three decisions carry forward on the same dates.

top3.topic: Ramayana film, day 11: the window is still open
top3.signal: Box-office headlines are new again today and the Ramayana page on English Wikipedia is at 2.91x its median. The radar's step for this week is the fact-check long-form.
top3.recommendation: This is decision 1. The hour it publishes, pin it under the three Ravana Shorts and both Ramayana long-forms. Judge it on day three, not day one.

top3.topic: Tipu Sultan, 20 November: the next dated moment, no Short scripted
top3.signal: Correction: the radar tags the day as his birth anniversary and yesterday's brief followed it. The owner's note says the birth date is disputed, so neither the title nor the script should claim the birthday.
top3.source: Moments radar, controversy news, owner's note of 15 November
top3.recommendation: Decision 2, in dates: script on 16 and 17 November, record on 18, publish by Friday 20 November before 18:00 IST, judge on day three. Name the men who took the treasure in sentence one, and tell the event whole: the film Shorts that answered a single scene brought reach without subscribers.

top3.topic: Guru Tegh Bahadur, 24 November: no Short scripted
top3.signal: The top-ranked dated moment on the radar, eight days out; its next step falls on 17 November. The day is a public observance.
top3.recommendation: Decision 3, in dates: sources by 17 November, script by 19, record by 21, publish on the evening of 23 November, judge on 26. The lesson on file: “Name the event, not the theme; and do not publish on the festival day itself.”

more.topic: 4 December: Bentinck's sati regulation of 1829, with a script already written
more.signal: On the radar 18 days out; its first step opens on 20 November. The tool lists a Short script on English wife-selling set against sati, written on 17 September and not recorded. Itiha's sati Short of 22 October has 1,719 views, so the subject alone does not carry.
more.source: Moments radar, scripts on disk, own Analytics
more.recommendation: Not a decision this week. On 20 November reread the script: if sentence one is a dated sale with a price and a place, record it for 3 December; if it opens on an argument, leave it.

skipped.recommendation: Skip the second illustration Short that yesterday's brief held open. The first did not widen and the week is full.

whats_working: The best converter in the 90-day window is still “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History” at 12.1 net subscribers per 1,000 views. Its lesson is the shape of the Ravana long-form: “Name the villain, convict him with a document or payment he cannot deny, then end on who is still repeating him today.”

Ravana is what viewers are choosing: “Why Ravana Kidnapped Sita: The Scene the Ramayana Movie Skipped” has 74,487 views at 77.2% average view, and “Was Ravana Good or Bad? The Ramayana Movie Controversy Began in 1882” has 29,606.
The growth now rests on videos. Uploads brought 475 of the channel's 840 net subscribers over 28 days, and long-form brought 330 of those against 145 from Shorts.
whats_wrong: Long-form is running out and nothing is ready to follow it. “Ramayana’s Many Versions” stands at 8,268 views and 1.1 net subscribers per 1,000 a week after release. Probable cause, from its post-mortem: “When the hook names a conflict, the next sentence must stay inside it.” Test: in the Ravana long-form the minute after the opening stays with the opening's man; compare the drop at 0:35.

Reach from the film is not turning into subscribers. “Why Ravana Kidnapped Sita” brings 0.2 net subscribers per 1,000 views and the Asia long-form 2. Long-form's rate over the 365-day window has dropped to 8.5, out of its usual range, now that one video is 42.3% of long-form views in that window; only 41.2% of November's long-form views were engaged views, so part of this is the count. Probable cause: every film video answers one scene or tours a map, and none names a culprit. Test: the Ravana long-form on the same traffic; compare per 1,000 on day three.

The line planned as the long-form's opening already lost viewers once. In “Was Ravana Good or Bad?” 17 points left at 0:06, on the words “1882 when a British administrator called”. Probable cause: a date and a job title before the viewer knows what the man did. The lesson on file: “Opening on a credentials biography loses more viewers than any other open on the channel; start at the moment the evidence appears.” Test: open on what the book says, name the author after, and compare the first 30 seconds.

“Why Is Lord Rama in the Original Constitution of India?” did not widen: 1,244 views three days on, under the usual for a Short, though its like rate is 8.8% against a Shorts median of 3.9%. It lost 13 points at 0:05, where the script turns from the question to describing the manuscript. Probable cause: the first five seconds give the feed no person and no quarrel. Test: no second Constitution Short on this pattern.

actions.action: Change the channel's own comment under “Why Ravana Kidnapped Sita”, which sends viewers to “Ramayana’s Many Versions”, to point at “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History” until the Ravana long-form is up.
actions.rationale: The video it points to brings 1.1 net subscribers per 1,000 views since release; the other brings 12.1 in the 90-day window.

actions.action: Answer the Chola correction under the Asia long-form and pin the answer.
actions.rationale: It is the most-liked correction on the channel's largest long-form, and acknowledging Rajendra Chola's fleet costs one comment.

actions.action: Check “Itihasa vs Myth” and “Is Caste Unique to India?” in Studio for visibility history and restrictions.
actions.rationale: They stand at 74 and 247 views two weeks on, with days of zero after publish. Still open from yesterday.

growth.verdict: Needs 226 net subscribers a day. The channel does 31/day, so the target is a **7.3x** change in rate. Every lever this channel has demonstrated, pulled at once (scenario "4. Scenario 3 plus one breakout a quarter"), reaches 32.6/day — still 6.9x short. At that ceiling rate 100,000 arrives on 2033-10-23, 6.9 years out.

scenarios.name: 1. Current rate, nothing changes
assumptions: Measured: channel_totals_daily, everything the channel publishes, last 28 days.
Same formats, same cadence, same lane mix.
Includes the channel's one breakout: "Chakla: How the British Raj Created a ‘Licensed Vice’ System" is 1276 of the 2,813 subscribers that 21 fresh long-form videos produced.

scenarios.name: 2. Stop Shorts, same effort into long-form (no breakout)
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 12.5/day (350 of 806 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Measured: 21 long-form and 104 Shorts published in the last 365 days.
ASSUMPTION (not measured): 6 Shorts cost what 1 long-form costs, so the Shorts become 17.3 more long-form videos a year — 38.3 in total.
Measured: MEDIAN 32 subscribers per fresh long-form video. The mean is 134, inflated by one breakout, so the median is the honest number for planned output.
Gives up the 449 subscribers a year the Shorts brought in; they are simply absent from this total.
Below scenario 1 because scenario 1 contains a breakout and this one does not. That is the point, not an error.

scenarios.name: 3. All long-form, all revision lane (no breakout)
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 12.5/day (350 of 806 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Scenario 2's cadence, every topic chosen from the revision lane.
Measured on the same fresh set: 8 revision long-form videos, median 58 subscribers, against 32 for fresh long-form overall.
ASSUMPTION: the lane median holds as output scales. It rests on a small number of videos and is the weakest link here.

scenarios.name: 4. Scenario 3 plus one breakout a quarter
assumptions: Carries the non-upload baseline of 12.5/day (350 of 806 net subscribers over 28 days came from no video). ASSUMPTION: it continues. It currently rests on one viral community post, so treat it as the least safe number here.
Scenario 3, plus four videos a year performing like the best video the channel has ever published.
Measured: "Chakla: How the British Raj Created a ‘Licensed Vice’ System" brought 1,276 subscribers on 72,857 views.
ASSUMPTION: a breakout that size can be produced to order, four times a year. The channel has produced one.
